gaps.target_position: Tensions 1 and 2 / L2 residual: trained stated confidence (verbal head or RL-trained) on execution labels with AUROC reported is CLEAN (provisional) on code; pivot criterion 3 open, not triggered
search_queries: arXiv export API: abs:"verbalized confidence" AND abs:"code generation" AND (abs:"reinforcement learning" OR abs:"fine-tuning" OR abs:"calibration training")
arXiv export API: abs:"calibrated" AND abs:"code" AND abs:"unit tests" AND (abs:"reward" OR abs:"confidence head")
Semantic Scholar lookup (not search): citations of RLCR (Beyond Binary Rewards), ConfTuner, and Rewarding Doubt, screened for code or execution-graded tasks
gaps.rationale: Two loci rest the recommendation on this being unrun on code. A single code paper that trains stated confidence on execution labels and reports AUROC or Brier against a probe would trigger pivot 3 and reshape the L2 spine. The search is metadata only, so a miss stays an instrument gap. Use citation screens (lookup works) as the main route, not keyword search.

gaps.target_position: Probe-confound: controlled within-problem probe margin is at most about 0.05 AUROC on code; Ribeiro (2512.07404) probe advantage is uncontrolled
search_queries: Semantic Scholar lookup: full citation list of arXiv:2512.07404, paged, filtered for within-problem, difficulty-controlled, or input-only baseline analyses
Semantic Scholar lookup: citation list of arXiv:2608.08266 (robustness follow-up) and arXiv:2606.14530, read for supervision-matched readout baselines
arXiv export API: abs:"hidden states" AND abs:"code correctness" AND (abs:"difficulty" OR abs:"confound" OR abs:"prompt-only" OR abs:"within-problem")
gaps.rationale: The close-citer set is only four papers and was built from title and abstract recall. A full citation sweep of the occupant and its robustness follow-up is the one cheap instrument that works. It could find a study that already runs the difficulty-matched or supervision-matched control (which would make L2 OCCUPIED) or a larger within-problem margin than 0.05 (which would remove the premise for a null-result framing).

gaps.target_position: Update-after-failing-test (verbal confidence revision after an observed test failure, with spurious-failure and placebo arms) is CLEAN (provisional), 45 to 55 percent confidence

arXiv export API: abs:"verbalized confidence" AND abs:"feedback" AND (abs:"belief update" OR abs:"sycophancy" OR abs:"capitulation") AND abs:"code"

Semantic Scholar lookup: citations of Resist-and-Update (counterfactual report coordinates) and of Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation (2306.09896), screened for confidence after feedback
gaps.rationale: This is the lowest-confidence CLEAN call in the set and the nearest work is only non-code. Coding-agent and self-repair work often logs the model's self-assessment after a test result without framing it as calibration. A hit would change the hedged probe into a replication, or sharpen it.

gaps.target_position: L1 Q3 release-date split for calibration (not accuracy) is NARROW across non-verbal families; contamination effect on calibration residual rests on Tuerlings (verbal-only) and 2512.08810 (token-likelihood)
search_queries: arXiv export API: abs:"contamination" AND (abs:"calibration" OR abs:"overconfidence" OR abs:"uncertainty") AND abs:"code" AND (abs:"post-cutoff" OR abs:"release date" OR abs:"LiveCodeBench")
arXiv export API: abs:"memorization" AND abs:"confidence" AND abs:"code language models" AND abs:"calibration"
Semantic Scholar lookup: citations of LiveCodeBench (arXiv:2403.07974) and of Tuerlings (verbalized uncertainty, contamination-aware), screened for hidden-state or sampling-based confidence
gaps.rationale: Release-date control is the headline of L1. If a paper already compares probe, sampling, or token confidence across pre- and post-cutoff problems, the L1 residual shrinks to the label-oracle swap alone. The vault shows only two near neighbors, both single-family, which is thin for a CLEAN-leaning call.

gaps.target_position: L1 Q4 label independence and test-insufficiency effect on calibration: NARROW, supported by Liu 2609.25938 (SQL) and 2610.11300 (token-only, strengthened tests)
search_queries: arXiv export API: abs:"EvalPlus" OR abs:"HumanEval+" AND (abs:"calibration" OR abs:"ECE" OR abs:"AUROC") AND abs:"confidence" AND abs:"false positive"
arXiv export API: abs:"test insufficiency" OR abs:"weak tests" OR abs:"incorrect programs pass" AND abs:"uncertainty" AND abs:"code generation"

Semantic Scholar lookup: citations of 2610.11300 and of Liu 2609.25938, and of SWE-ABS (adversarial benchmark strengthening), screened for confidence-estimation rankings under original versus strengthened tests
gaps.rationale: The base versus augmented-test oracle swap is the most concrete, cheapest L1 control and the one the recommendation can run without new models. Support rests on two papers from other settings. A direct code study ranking confidence families under both test suites would move this to OCCUPIED. The loci notes flag the claim as untested, so independent confirmation or a miss is worth one fetch pass.
